samples.summary: No test covers the new frontend API-key behavior (section now visible to non-owner members, owner-only "Created by" column, creatorName fallback)
samples.evidence: The diff makes a substantive UI change: the API Keys section is no longer wrapped in `{isOwner && ...}`, the listing query is enabled for any member (`enabled: !!workspaceId`), a new owner-only `Created by` column renders `creatorName(apiKey.createdBy)` with an "Unknown" fallback, and the blurb text branches on `isOwner`. The only frontend test for this page, packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx, mocks `fetchApiKeys` (line 26) and never renders/asserts anything about API keys — its 'hides them from a non-owner member' case only checks member/invite controls. So a regression that hides the section from members again, or leaks the owner-only creator column to a plain member, would ship green. Note also packages/frontend has no `tsc` lane, so nothing else guards this file.

samples.summary: Newly reachable path — a member-minted API key acting on /api/v1 — has no test, though the diff's comments assert its authority limits
samples.evidence: Before this change only owners could mint keys, so every API-key request on /api/v1 carried owner authority. The diff opens minting to any member and rewrites the comments in folders.controller.ts (line 71-74) and documents.controller.ts (line 181-184) to claim 'a plain member's key renames but does not move or delete somebody else's folder' / 'a plain member's key deletes only their own documents'. I could not find any test exercising a member-minted Bearer key against /api/v1: packages/backend/test/api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts only ever mints keys as `owner` for the v1 cases ('full lifecycle', 'v1 document CRUD via API key'), and the new member-scoped case never uses its key as a Bearer token. If the manager check regressed, a member's key silently deleting another member's folders/documents would ship undetected.

samples.summary: The non-member cases in the controller spec only assert that a hand-written mock rejection propagates
samples.evidence: `workspaceService.assertMember` is a jest mock that rejects with ForbiddenException for any id other than 1 or 2 (spec lines 33-40). The tests 'still refuses a non-member' (line 56) and 'refuses a non-member before reaching the service' (line 96) therefore assert only that the controller awaits a mock that the test itself configured to reject — the real membership check is mocked away, so these cannot fail if the authorization logic in WorkspaceService or the controller's call ordering degrades in any way other than dropping the await entirely. The e2e spec's 'rejects API key management for non-members' is the test that actually covers this; the unit versions are near-tautological.

samples.summary: No test asserts the new `createdBy` field actually appears in the list response the frontend now depends on
samples.evidence: `list` gained `createdBy: true` in its select and the frontend's `ApiKey` interface declares `createdBy: number` and renders it. The service unit test asserts the select object shape against a mocked Prisma, but the e2e listing assertions (api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts lines 182-194) only map over `name`, so no test proves the serialized response actually carries `createdBy`. If it were dropped (e.g. by a DTO/serializer), the owner's 'Created by' column would silently show 'Unknown' and nothing would fail.

samples.summary: 'returns the revoked key without its hash' verifies the select literal, not that no hash reaches the caller
samples.evidence: With Prisma mocked, `result` is whatever `findUnique` was stubbed to return, so `expect(result).toEqual({id:'k1',name:'CI'})` re-asserts the stub. The meaningful part is `select.hashedKey` being undefined, which does catch an explicit `hashedKey: true`; it cannot catch the response being re-shaped elsewhere. No integration assertion checks a revoke response body for absence of `hashedKey`.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The behavior is real in workspace-settings.tsx: the API-keys query is enabled for any member (`enabled: !!workspaceId`, line 149), the section renders unconditionally (lines 432-505, unlike the isOwner-gated Danger Zone at 508), the "Created by" header/cell is owner-only (460, 473-477), `creatorName` falls back to "Unknown" (153-155), and the blurb branches on isOwner (439-441). No test anywhere covers it: a repo-wide grep for `creatorName|Created by` over packages/ yields only the source file; the sole page test (workspace-settings.test.tsx) mocks fetchApiKeys at line 26 and its three cases assert only member rows/remove buttons/invite controls (110-178), with the non-owner case (135-161) saying nothing about API keys. I searched beyond the reviewer's paths: packages/frontend/tests/** has no settings or API-key coverage, there are no frontend e2e .spec files (all 115 are backend), design-sandbox's workspace.ts (42-56) is a preview fixture not a test and lacks createdBy, and design-sandbox/test/scenes/manifest.test.ts only validates scene ids (line 155). Backend api-key specs cover server-side scoping and cannot catch a frontend visibility regression. Missing coverage over a role-dependent user-visible path = blocking major under this lens.

finding.summary: Newly reachable path — a member-minted API key acting on /api/v1 — has no test, though the diff's comments assert its authority limits
finding.evidence: Before this change only owners could mint keys, so every API-key request on /api/v1 carried owner authority. The diff opens minting to any member and rewrites the comments in folders.controller.ts (line 71-74) and documents.controller.ts (line 181-184) to claim 'a plain member's key renames but does not move or delete somebody else's folder' / 'a plain member's key deletes only their own documents'. I could not find any test exercising a member-minted Bearer key against /api/v1: packages/backend/test/api-key-http.e2e-spec.ts only ever mints keys as `owner` for the v1 cases ('full lifecycle', 'v1 document CRUD via API key'), and the new member-scoped case never uses its key as a Bearer token. verdict.reason: The finding asserts the member-minted-API-key authority limits documented in folders.controller.ts:71-74 and documents.controller.ts have no test. They are tested in the colocated unit specs the reviewer did not search (they looked in packages/backend/test and grepped for isManager|createdBy; the specs express the case as req(MEMBER, true)). folders.controller.spec.ts:82-83 builds a request with isApiKey=true for a given minter; :263-268 asserts a member-minted key cannot MOVE a folder it does not author (ForbiddenException AND folderService.update not called), :294-299 asserts the same for DELETE (delete not called), :169-176 covers the 'a plain member may still rename' half of the comment, :253-258/:286-292 cover the owner-key contrast and assert assertMember is consulted with the minter's id (the 'authority resolved now, not at mint time' claim), and :301-309 covers a minter removed from the workspace. documents.controller.spec.ts:91-97 mirrors this: a member-minted write-scoped key deleting someone else's document rejects with ForbiddenException and deleteDocument is not called; :80-86 covers the owner-key case and :256 a member key filing a document. These are not over-mocked for this purpose — the controller's isManager and the real isDocumentManager execute; only workspaceService.assertMember (the external dependency supplying the role) is stubbed, and both 'owner' and 'member' roles are exercised. So a regression in the manager check would fail existing tests. The residual true point is only that no HTTP-level e2e replays a member-minted Bearer key on /api/v1; that is narrower transport coverage, not an untested behavior, and does not meet this lens's 'no meaningful test' bar.
